results.content:
A new Economist/YouGov poll released Sept. 22 found Trump's approval rating fell five points in a single week, from 40% to 35%, wiping out five straight weeks of gains in the same poll. The drop leaves him just two points above the lowest rating he's ever recorded in the survey and comes as Republicans enter the final stretch before November's midterm elections. [...] The Economist/YouGov survey was conducted Sept. 18-21 among 1,402 registered voters and has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.4 percentage points.

results.content: Using YouGov’s data, The Economist has projected Mr Trump’s approval rating state by state. As you might expect, approval of Mr Trump is lowest in states that tend to vote for Democrats and highest in those that tend to vote for Republicans. Mr Trump’s voters still overwhelmingly approve of his performance as president. But the projection also shows how dissatisfaction with Mr Trump is widespread even in states that voted for him in 2024. The numbers will make anxious reading for Republicans [...] Donald Trump likes a grand show. His recent summit with Xi Jinping, China’s leader, had pomp, pageantry—and little substance. results.content: Perhaps most importantly, polls are showing Trump losing ground steadily among swing-voter groups that helped him return to the White House in 2024. Economist-YouGov shows 22 percent of 2024 Trump voters now disapproving of his job performance. results.content:
Meanwhile, the latest polling shows Trump with some of the lowest approval ratings he's received.

A Sept. 16-20 American Research Group poll showed just 29% approval and disapproval ratings of 68%. In a Sept. 18-21 Economist/YouGov poll, Trump saw a 62% disapproval rating — and 58% disapproval of his ban on the three networks from the White House. In Michigan, a Sept. 22 Civiqs poll found a 58% disapproval rating of Trump's job performance.
